final_answer.evidence_summary: candidate_13 is feasible and lower cost than the optimized higher-activity candidates. All non-optimized candidates are dominated by candidate_13 under the declared screening rule because their reference activity is lower and metal price is higher. The highest-activity candidate_04 would need a 201.2x intrinsic activity improvement to reach candidate_13 cost parity, while the frozen descriptor manifold offers only 1.09x at reference, so parity by intrinsic activity alone is unreachable.

chosen_args.why_stop: S1 satisfied by feasible optimized candidate_13; S2 satisfied by optimizing candidate_04 and candidate_05 and screening all remaining candidates by lower activity plus higher price relative to candidate_13; S3 satisfied by BACKWARD and TEST_REACHABILITY for highest-activity candidate_04. Remaining budget cannot pay for meaningful validation/MC actions; best affordable action has negligible decision value.

risks: Process window was a broad affordable subset rather than the full admissible P/T/Tsep domain; candidate_13 optimum has Tsep_C=30 at the warm separator edge of the selected/full domain, so a formal window-edge validity check would have been useful but costs 28 CU and is unaffordable.
Descriptor uncertainty was read but not propagated by MC because the cheapest useful MC exceeds remaining budget.

candidate_04 and candidate_05 optimized bed volumes are very small, so vessel-correlation floor validation would be useful for exact model validity but is unaffordable; however these candidates are already more expensive than candidate_13 in the canonical optimization.
Exact state-level dominance checks were not run for screened candidates because each costs 28 CU; the declared screening rule is satisfied.
